Operator ruling 2026-08-23: "There are two blank lines at the bottom and one is just a flashing prompt cursor. I don't need the blanks and I do not want to see the flashing cursor." Four causes were already located in untracked/watch-fleet.sh; each fixed in place, plus the test suite extended red-first. (1) Leading blank above the footer: the footer printf began with '
' — removed, the line above the footer is now the frame's last data row. (2) Trailing newline plus unhidden cursor: the same printf ended with '
', parking the cursor on the line below the footer (the flashing line) — removed; the footer is now the terminal's last line and the cursor sits on it, hidden. (3) Cursor never hidden/restored: added one hide (\033[?25l, the tput civis sequence, printed once before the loop) guarded by [ -t 1 ] so one-shot/piped output stays escape-free; the restore (\033[?25h, the tput cnorm sequence) lives in cleanup ONLY, as the brief requires, also tty-guarded. cleanup gained an idempotency flag (CLEANED): every exit path (q, INT, TERM, HUP, one-shot) calls cleanup explicitly AND the EXIT trap fires it again, so without the flag the newline+restore would emit twice on q and ^C (a second blank line at exit). The HUP trap's own 'printf "
"' was removed — cleanup now owns the exit newline (one fresh line for the shell prompt, standard full-screen-app exit behavior). (4) Reserve: T739's reserve=$(( 2*k - 1 + 2 + 1 )) counted a 2-line footer plus a '+1 spare'; the spare existed to park the trailing-newline cursor row, which no longer exists. Re-derived from what the frame actually prints: k headings + (k-1) separators + 1 one-line footer + one '(more)' per flexible section over its MIN_ROWS floor — reserve=$(( 2*k - 1 + 1 )), spare dropped, no magic +1 left (comment explains why it is no longer load-bearing). TEST-FIRST per the standing method: arms K/L/M were written before the fix and run RED against the pre-fix live file, GREEN after. Arm K re-pinned: 40-row terminal with 20 DONE + 20 OPEN now shows 17+17=34 rows in a 39-line one-shot frame (interactive = 40 exactly, footer on the last line) vs T739's 16+16=32 / 37 — the two rows recovered are the leading blank and the trailing-newline cursor row; the arm additionally asserts one-shot piped output carries no ?25l/?25h escapes (the hide/restore are tty-guarded). Arm L (new, pty via `script -q /dev/null`): draws one frame then q; asserts the hide sequence is present, the output ENDS with the restore sequence, the last non-empty line IS the footer (no trailing blank), the line above the footer is a data row (no leading blank), and the visible frame fits FLEET_LINES=24. Arm M (new): ^C after one frame; asserts exit code 130, hide present, output ends with the restore (the trap path is the one that gets forgotten), and the footer rendered before the ^C. The pty harness was verified manually before authoring: `script` on macOS tees the session to both the file argument and stdout, so the arms pass /dev/null as the file and capture stdout only; a 0.5 s delay before sending q lets stty -echo land so the key never echoes into the capture.
